structured.name: The Bahamas
structured._source: wikidata (CC0); landBorders + naturalResources from CIA World Factbook (public domain)

prose.hook: This is a chain of islands scattered across the North Atlantic, southeast of Florida and northeast of Cuba, with no land borders of any kind since it doesn't touch the Caribbean Sea at all — despite that, it's usually grouped as a Caribbean nation. Of its extensive island chain, only about 30 are inhabited, and its position adjacent to the US and Cuba gives it a strategic location.
prose.physicalGeography: The islands are built from long, flat coral formations, broken up by some low rounded hills rather than dramatic relief.
prose.climate: The climate is tropical marine, kept moderate by the warm waters of the Gulf Stream. Hurricanes and other tropical storms are a real hazard, causing extensive flood and wind damage.
prose.economy: The Bahamas runs a high-income economy built on tourism and financial services, though major income inequality persists alongside that wealth. Strong bilateral ties with the US and several tax relief programs support the economy, and there's targeted investment in agriculture, energy, light manufacturing, and technology to diversify it. Key industries include tourism, banking, oil bunkering, maritime industries, transshipment and logistics, salt, aragonite, and pharmaceuticals, with exports led by refined petroleum, ships, aluminum, shellfish, and plastics.
prose.peopleAndCulture: English is the official language, with Creole spoken among Haitian immigrants. The population is predominantly Protestant, with Baptist, Anglican, and Pentecostal the largest denominations, alongside a Roman Catholic minority and other Christian groups. In terms of ancestry, the population is 90.6% of African descent, with smaller White and mixed-heritage communities.
